preservation_scope: Exact tool names/arguments, selected response metadata and explicit failures. Long paper text/abstracts are not redistributed.

arguments.query: Find the primary cosmological recombination paper by Seager Sasselov Scott that gives the matter temperature evolution equation with Compton coupling 8 sigma_T a_R T_gamma^4 divided by 3 m_e c, electron fraction over 1 plus helium abundance plus electron fraction, and adiabatic cooling.
arguments.objective: Return original research papers or author-hosted arXiv manuscripts that explicitly state the nonrelativistic gas Compton temperature equation and its heat-capacity convention. Prefer the original RECFAST matter-temperature equation; exclude blogs and derivative tutorials. Need equation location and source version.

arguments.searchQuestion: Which primary cosmological recombination calculations derive the gas matter-temperature evolution from nonrelativistic Compton scattering, including the factor 8 sigma_T a_R T_gamma^4/(3 m_e c) times the free-electron fraction divided by total particle abundance, and explain the equilibrium limit T_m=T_gamma?

calls.resolution: Selected arXiv paper was read directly. Official arXiv identifies 2009-04-21 v2; the repository-style 2022 discovery metadata is not used as the publication date.

selected_response_metadata.title: A New Calculation of the Recombination Epoch

calls.observation: Primary publisher text confirms a simultaneous matter-temperature equation containing adiabatic and Compton terms. Its text extraction omits image-based equations; the exact coefficient was verified in Scott–Moss Eq (2), and the Exa result's ar5iv mathematical rendering.

selected_response_metadata.mathematical_content: (1+z) dTm/dz=(Tm-Tr)/(H tC)+2Tm; tC=3 me c/(8 sigmaT aR Tr^4)*(1+fHe+xe)/xe.

calls.consequence: No repeated attempt of the same disabled path. The successful primary publisher retrieval and separate Scott–Moss primary PDF supply the selected confirmation.

not_claimed: No adoption of unrelated recombination or tight-coupling switching algorithms.
